name: AT42QT1070-SSUR
title: AT42QT1070: seven-channel QTouch capacitive touch sensor IC, I2C or standalone, SOIC-14 and VQFN-20
summary: A capacitive touch controller that senses up to seven keys by charge transfer, one pin per key and no external sampling capacitor. In comms mode an I2C host (fixed address 0x1B, 400 kHz) sets thresholds, averaging, integrators, AKS groups, guard channel and low-power interval, and reads status prompted by an open-drain CHANGE line. In standalone mode four keys plus a guard key drive five open-drain outputs with fixed settings. It runs from 1.8 V to 5.5 V over –40 °C to +85 °C, with built-in calibration, drift compensation and noise filtering.
key_figures: 525 µA at 3.3 V, LP mode 2; 211 µA at 1.8 V, LP mode 6
I2C, 400 kHz, address 0x1B; or five open-drain outputs

circuits.title: Typical circuit, comms mode (SOIC-14)
circuits.description: Seven touch keys run by an I2C host. MODE is grounded so the chip starts in comms mode. Each key electrode connects to its KEYn pin through a series resistor Rs. SDA, SCL, CHANGE and RESET each have a pull-up to Vdd; SDA and SCL go to the host's bus, CHANGE tells the host to read the status bytes, and RESET may be driven by the host. C1 decouples the supply at the chip.
notes: Rs is 4.7 kΩ to 20 kΩ, C1 a 0.1 µF ceramic, RSDA and RSCL 1 kΩ to 10 kΩ, RCHG 47 kΩ. RRST has no specified value.

circuits.title: Typical circuit, standalone mode (SOIC-14)
circuits.description: Five touch keys with no host. MODE is tied to Vdd so the chip starts in standalone mode with its fixed settings, key 0 acting as the guard channel. Each electrode connects to its KEYn pin through a series resistor Rs. Each open-drain output OUT0 to OUT4 reaches the outside through a series resistor, with an optional capacitor to Vss at the far side. RESET has a pull-up R1 to Vdd. C1 decouples the supply at the chip.
notes: Rs is 4.7 kΩ to 20 kΩ and C1 a 0.1 µF ceramic. R1, the output resistors and the output capacitors have no specified values; COUT0 to COUT4 are optional.

operation.text: Each key is measured by bursts of charge-transfer pulses using a dual-pulse acquisition, so a key needs only one pin and no external sampling capacitor (Cs). Burst timing is spread-spectrum modulated (chirp, ±8 %, 162 kHz to 198 kHz sample frequency) to reject outside noise and reduce emissions. Outputs are debounced inside the chip.

MODE is read at power-up. Tied to VSS it gives comms mode: up to seven keys (or six plus a guard channel), every setting programmable over I2C and status read from registers. Tied to VDD it gives standalone mode: four keys plus a guard channel fixed on key 0, settings fixed in firmware, and each key's state shown on an open-drain output OUT0 to OUT4 able to drive an LED. Comms mode has no general-purpose I/O.
Standalone mode fixes the guard key (key 0) at AVE 16 with a 10-count threshold, and keys 1 to 4 at a 20-count threshold. Max On Duration is about 30 s.
In comms mode a key that is not used is disabled by writing an averaging factor of 0. Disabled keys read 0 in the key status register.

The chip works on a base cycle of about 8 ms; the LP register (address 54) sets how many base cycles pass between measurements, 255 choices from 8 ms to 2.040 s. Longer intervals draw less current and respond more slowly. During calibration, touch and the detect-integrator count the chip runs at LP mode 1 for speed. Settings above 32 (256 ms) slow thermal drift compensation and suit only designs without fast temperature changes.

Keys can be put into up to three AKS groups (bits 1–0 of each AVE/AKS register; 0 means no group). Within a group only one key can be in detect at a time: the one with the largest signal change, and no other key in that group enters detect until it is released. Keys in different groups, or in no group, can be in detect together.

Comms mode only. CHANGE is open drain and active low; it falls when the detection status or key status bytes change and floats high again once the host reads them. If the status returns to its earlier value before the host reads it (a quick touch and release), CHANGE stays low until any register is read. A 47 kΩ pull-up to VDD is used. Reading only on CHANGE, rather than polling, lets the chip sleep longest, since I2C traffic wakes it. CHANGE is pulled low 100 ms after each power-up or reset.

RESET has an internal 60 kΩ pull-up and may be tied to VDD or driven by a logic line; the minimum pulse width is 5 µs. Any nonzero write to the RESET register (address 57) starts the watchdog, which resets the chip 125 ms later. For the first 30 ms of initialisation the chip NACKs every I2C access. The power-up delay to operation and calibration is under 230 ms, longer when bursts are very long.

Any nonzero write to the calibrate register (address 56) recalibrates all keys, which clears a key stuck in detect. CALIBRATE (bit 7, address 2) stays set while it runs. Calibration clears every key status bit and the overflow bit.

One key can be the guard channel: fixed on key 0 in standalone mode, chosen by bits 3–0 of address 53 in comms mode (0 to 6; a larger value turns the guard off). The guard electrode is larger, so more sensitive, and is given a higher averaging factor and lower threshold than the other keys. When the guard begins filtering into detect, any other key's detect filter is reset, and a guard detection overrides the other keys.

A key enters detect when its signal moves from its reference by the negative threshold NTHR (default 20 counts) for the detect-integrator count. The reference drifts slowly to follow the environment: one step per 2.88 s toward touch and per 0.96 s away from touch at an 8 ms cycle. NTHR must not be 0, which would put a key in detect with its signal equal to its reference.

A key must be confirmed in detect on DI consecutive measurements (default 4, minimum 2; 0 and 1 act as 2) before it is reported. The same integrator applies on release; with the FO bit (bit 5 of address 53) set, every key leaves detect after 4 measurements whatever its DI.

Cx, the capacitance of a key, works best from 1 pF to 30 pF; larger Cx lowers sensitivity. Keys can be 6 mm × 6 mm or larger, under up to 10 mm of glass or 5 mm of plastic, depending on electrode size; electrodes may be etched copper, silver, carbon or ITO on one layer.

A detection that lasts longer than the Max On Duration triggers recalibration, so an object resting on a key does not block it for good. With the MAX CAL bit (bit 4 of address 53) clear all keys recalibrate; with it set only the key that timed out does.
If a key's signal steps in the negative direction from its reference by more than 4 counts (the positive recalibration setting), that key recalibrates.
While any key is in detect, drift is held on all keys, and for about 4 s after the last touch ends. This keeps a finger near a dense keypad from shifting the references of the keys around it.

AVE (bits 7–2 of addresses 39–45) is the number of pulses summed and averaged into each signal value; it is limited to 1, 2, 4, 8, 16 or 32. More pulses improve SNR and lengthen acquisition. The OVERFLOW bit sets when acquiring all keys takes longer than 8 ms.
Each key line carries a series resistor Rs of about 4.7 kΩ to 20 kΩ, which limits ESD current, suppresses RF interference and reduces noise.

Fast digital lines near sense traces and electrodes add transients that lower SNR: keep them away, or keep them still during bursts. An LED terminal that is switched or multiplexed into a floating state, inside or very near a key (even on another board), needs a bypass of at least 10 nF to VSS or VDD; any capacitor type works and its position is not critical. LED terminals held at VSS or VDD need nothing.

No-clean flux is normally fine, but rework can turn its residue into a moisture-absorbing film whose leakage upsets the measurement. Clean a reworked board thoroughly round the sensor parts and dry it before testing.

Supply 1.8 V to 5.5 V with ripple and noise within ±25 mV. Slow supply changes are tracked by drift compensation; fast ones cause sensitivity errors or false detections. A separate regulator is preferred; sharing a regulator with other logic is not advised, though an extra LDO is not normally needed. Place one 0.1 µF ceramic capacitor right at the supply pins with short traces, or the chip may oscillate, draw high current and behave erratically; a larger capacitor (about 1 µF) is assumed elsewhere on the rail.

Comms mode only. The fixed 7-bit address is 0x1B; the clock runs up to 400 kHz. A write sends the register address then data bytes, which go to consecutive addresses; addresses 0x00 to 0x7F are acknowledged, but only 0x20 to 0x39 hold writable memory. A read sets the address with a write (address below 0x80), then a STOP and START or a repeated START with the read bit; the chip sends bytes from successive addresses until the host NACKs. The address pointer returns to the last address written, so repeated reads of one location need no new address. The chip stretches SCL when it needs time. Every transfer must end with a STOP.
SDA and SCL are open drain and need pull-ups to VDD, typically 1 kΩ to 10 kΩ, chosen so rise times stay within the 1 µs I2C limit.
